answers.answer: 2 players: 4 Player cards each; 3 players: 3 each; 4 players: 2 each. Epidemic cards are removed and set aside before dealing; matching pawns start in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Remove Epidemic cards and set aside’; starting-hands table; ‘Place matching colored pawns in Atlanta.’

answers.answer: Place the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2 space. Reveal 3 Infection cards and place 3 matching cubes on each named city; reveal 3 more and place 2 each; reveal 3 more and place 1 each. Put all 9 revealed cards on the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: ‘leftmost “2” space’; three groups of three cards with 3, 2, and 1 cubes; 9 cards to discard pile, remainder Infection Deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles, as equal in size as possible; shuffle one Epidemic into each pile and stack them with smaller piles on the bottom. The summary does not state what to do with any unused Epidemic cards.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7 specifies the difficulty counts, equal-as-possible piles, one Epidemic per pile, and smaller piles on the bottom; unused Epidemics are not addressed.

answers.answer: You may take up to 4 actions and may repeat an action. Whether you may stop early is not specified. The summary does not state where cards discarded to pay action costs go. Then draw 2 Player cards, resolve Epidemics, and discard down to 7; next infect cities, then play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Do 4 Actions’ (actions ‘may repeat’), then draw 2 and infect cities; ‘After completing all 3 phases, play passes to the left.’

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry moves to a city connected by a white line; a white line crossing the board edge wraps to the other edge. Direct Flight requires discarding the City card naming the destination. Charter Flight requires discarding the City card matching the city you are in and moves to any city. Shuttle Flight requires being in a city with a research station and moves to any other city with a research station.
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table gives the movement conditions and card costs; Special Rules says white lines going off an edge wrap to the other edge.

answers.answer: Normally discard the City card matching your current city to place a research station there. If all 6 are built, move one from the board. Any extra stations supplied are set aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Build a Research Station action; Special Rules: ‘Only 6 exist’ and ‘If more than 6 stations supplied: Set extras aside during setup.’

answers.answer: A non-Medic removes 1 cube of any color from their city with one Treat Disease action; if that disease is cured, remove all cubes of that color in the city. This means one action can remove a single cube of one color, or all cubes of one cured color, not cubes of multiple colors. The destination of removed cubes is not stated.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: ‘Remove 1 disease cube of any color from your city. If that disease is cured, remove all cubes of that color from your city instead.’

answers.answer: At a research station, discard 5 City cards of the same color to cure that disease; the station city need not match the disease color. What happens to existing cubes, and whether/how a cure can be discovered when no cubes of that color are on the board, are not specified.
answers.evidence: Discover a Cure action requires a research station and 5 same-color City cards; Special Rules says the city color need not match. No-cube and existing-cube effects are not stated.

answers.answer: The card must be the City card matching the city both players occupy. They must both agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they must immediately discard or play an Event card. The summary does not specify a distinct rule for a recipient who reaches exactly 8 cards, but its hand-limit rule applies immediately after receiving cards.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge action and Hand Limit: both players in same city, ‘Both players must agree,’ and excess cards must immediately be discarded or played as Events.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card to a player in the same city. A player sharing with the Researcher on their own turn may take any of the Researcher’s City cards. The summary does not establish whether another player may give the Researcher an arbitrary nonmatching card under this exception; it only describes a player taking a card from the Researcher.
answers.evidence: Roles: Researcher may give any City card; ‘A player who Shares Knowledge with the Researcher on their turn may take any of the Researcher's City cards.’

answers.answer: After completing actions, draw 2 Player cards. If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends and players lose; the two cards are drawn from the top, but whether they are drawn together or one at a time is not specified. Discards are not reshuffled.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: ‘Draw the top 2 cards’; if fewer than 2 remain, lose; ‘do not reshuffle discards.’

answers.answer: Resolve Increase, Infect, then Intensify. Increase the Infection Rate marker one space. For Infect, draw the bottom Infection card; place 3 matching cubes unless the disease is eradicated. The summary says that if the city already has cubes of that color, add only enough to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs; thus its stated result for a city with two cubes is one additional cube and an outbreak. Discard that Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. For Intensify, reshuffle only the Infection Discard Pile and place it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic card from the game; do not draw a replacement.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards section lists the three steps and says ‘If the city already has cubes of that color, add only enough to reach 3, then an outbreak occurs’; resolved Epidemics are removed and not replaced.
Infection Rate Track table: Epidemics resolved 0–6 maps to cards flipped 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.

answers.answer: Resolve all three steps for the first Epidemic, then all three for the second; Events may be played between them. The summary says to discard down to 7 after drawing Player cards, but does not specify when hand-limit reduction occurs relative to resolving two Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: ‘If 2 Epidemic cards are drawn at once, resolve all 3 steps for the first, then all 3 steps for the second. Events may be played between the two.’ Turn Structure says resolve Epidemics and discard down to 7, without further timing.

answers.answer: Flip cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For each normal disease, place 1 matching cube in the named city; if that city already has 3 of that color, do not add a fourth and cause an outbreak. If the disease is eradicated, place no cube. The summary does not specify whether a cured but non-eradicated disease receives a cube. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of deck, current infection rate, one at a time; place 1 cube, skip eradicated diseases, outbreak if city already has 3, discard each card. No effect for cured-but-not-eradicated diseases is stated.

answers.answer: An outbreak advances the Outbreaks marker one space and spreads one cube to every connected city. If a connected city already has 3 cubes of that color, its chain-reaction outbreak occurs after the current outbreak resolves and advances the marker again. During chain reactions, do not add cubes to cities that already had an outbreak while resolving that Infection card, so spread does not return into the first city once it has had an outbreak. Different colors each may have up to 3 cubes in a city; the cap is per color.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: marker advances; chain reactions occur after current outbreak resolves; no cubes added to cities already outbroken during the Infection card; cities can have multiple colors, up to 3 of each.

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played between drawing an Infection card and resolving it, so it cannot move the Quarantine Specialist before that outbreak. After the current card has resolved, an Event may be played before the next card: Events can be played at any time, subject to that restriction. The Event player chooses its use; Airlift moves any one pawn to any city, with permission for another player's pawn; it costs no action. Played Events go to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: any player may play at any time, but not between drawing and resolving a card; player decides use; Airlift effect; not an action; played Events to Player Discard Pile.

answers.answer: As an action, take 1 Event card from the Player Discard Pile and store it on the Contingency Planner role card. Only one may be stored, and it does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game instead of discarding it. How far down the discard pile is eligible is not specified.
answers.evidence: Roles, Contingency Planner: ‘As an action, take 1 Event card from the Player Discard Pile’; limit 1; not against hand limit; when played remove from game.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn (with its owner’s permission) to a city with another pawn, or move another player’s pawn as if it were their own. Direct/Charter Flight discards come from the Dispatcher’s hand; a Charter Flight card matches the city the Dispatcher is in. Whether the Dispatcher may direct another pawn to Treat Disease is not specified. The Dispatcher cannot use the Operations Expert’s special move.
answers.evidence: Dispatcher role description gives both movement options, permission, own-hand flight discards, and the Operations Expert restriction. Treatment of another pawn is not addressed.

answers.answer: Players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; diseases need not be eradicated and cubes may remain. The three losses are: the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (8th outbreak); the required number of cubes of a needed color cannot be placed, including during epidemics, outbreaks, or infections, causing an immediate loss; or a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after actions because fewer than 2 remain.
answers.evidence: Victory: cure all 4 immediately; eradication is not required and cubes may remain. Defeat lists the three triggers; Cube supply check specifies immediate loss during epidemic, outbreak, or infection.
